data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($280M) as a proxy for implied post-money valuation at Series B, application of a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement yields $476M. A peer-median approach could not be applied; while 5 same-sector companies exist in the comp universe, none meet the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints when filtered by stage, timing, or valuation tier, making sector-wide medians unreliable without introducing material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $405M (low) to $547M (high), with a median point of $476M. This single-method triangulation carries notable uncertainty: the stage-progression assumption that Quantum Machines will command typical Series C multipliers depends on execution relative to peer cohort and quantum computing sector maturation timelines, neither of which are directly quantified in available data. The thinness of precedent transactions in quantum computing at equivalent scale further limits validation confidence.
